source_artifacts.command: python -m src.pipeline.step3.train_fusion --dataset ton_iot --use-head-logits --output-dir data/ton_iot/processed/step3_fusion_head && python -m src.pipeline.step4.assemble_ladder --dataset ton_iot --use-llm-head --fusion-dir data/ton_iot/processed/step3_fusion_head

limitations: Edges are aggregated with the attack label in the grouping key, so these are not deployment-valid estimates.
Macro-F1 is over 8 eval classes (dos and ransomware dropped for support); not comparable to the UNSW 10-class ladder.
The ladder does NOT hold: AGAF ties the LLM (CI crosses zero) and the feedback loop sits BELOW both, by a margin whose CI excludes zero.
AGAF reproduces the trained LLM head almost exactly; the GNN branch adds no measurable lift on top of it.
The graph has 2127 edges; rare eval classes have 12-35 edges, so single-seed differences between fusion mechanisms are not resolvable (see the 2026-08-17 report).
The gate-entropy regulariser is still active at lambda=0.01, which rewards an uninformative gate; its effect has not been isolated.
